result.result:
The app is built and working: `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` runs it, and logging in with `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard. I drove it end to end in headless Chrome at 1280px and 390px, and the console showed no errors or warnings.

**What was checked in the browser:**
- **Login:** an empty submit puts both fields into an error state with a message. Wrong credentials are rejected; correct ones set `isLoggedIn` and redirect to `/dashboard`.
- **Guards:** opening `/dashboard` while logged out goes to `/login`, and opening `/login` while logged in goes to `/dashboard`. Sign Out clears the flag.
- **User menu:** it opens leftward and stays inside the viewport at both widths. It closes on an outside click.
- **CRUD:** editing a user (rename and role change via `PUT`), inviting one (`POST`) and deleting one (`DELETE`) all showed up in the table after reload. "Delete user" in the edit dialog opens the confirmation with the right member still selected.
- **Dialogs:** all four open and close, the delete confirmation closes on a backdrop click, and the invite form shows required-field errors.
- **Logs:** the log viewer adds a line every 3 seconds.

**How I worked without the agent docs:** `llms.client.txt` was absent from the start and still is; I never opened it. I worked out the library from its README, the `.d.ts` typings and the compiled templates. I used its header, footer, buttons, inputs, checkbox, dropdown, tags, avatar, table, list and modal. The user menu, dashboard tiles, bar chart, log viewer and dialog layouts are built locally. Styles reference only the `--ds-decisions-*` tokens, with no hard-coded hex values. The token stylesheet is imported in `src/styles.css`.

**Workarounds for gaps in the library** (all in `src/styles.css` or the shell, each with a comment):
- **Header:** it has no slot for a user control, so the profile menu sits on top of the header's right edge, aligned to its width. Below 640px the brand text and user name are hidden so the nav doesn't run under the menu.
- **Links:** the header and footer render plain links, which would reload the page. The shell intercepts clicks on them and routes through Angular instead.
- **Modal dropdown:** the modal body scrolls, which cut off the Role dropdown. The body now lets it overflow, but only while a dropdown is open.

**Where I followed the spec instead of Figma:**
- **Login text:** Figma's title is "Blueprint" / "Sign in to your account"; I used the spec's wording.
- **Dashboard tiles:** Figma has different tiles and values (for example 2,847 users, an hourly chart, no Data Summary tile); I used the spec's eight. The layout is four metric tiles, then chart / Service Health / Data Summary in one row, then System Logs full width.
- **Header:** I left out Figma's "Online" badge and its Overview/Metrics/Logs/Settings links. The nav is Dashboard and Team Members, so `/users` can be reached.
- **Users table:** Figma combines avatar and name into one column; I used the spec's separate Avatar and Name columns. Action emphasis also follows the spec (Details least, Edit secondary), the reverse of Figma.
- **Footer:** Figma shows a thin bar with just the copyright and legal links. The spec asks for brand and link columns too, so I used the library footer with placeholder links.

**Visual choices you should check:**
- **No exact token match:**
  - Values render at 22px; Figma uses 26px.
  - Tile shadows reuse the dropdown shadow token.
  - The page background reuses the hover-surface token, which happens to match Figma's #F5F5F5.
- **Library defaults kept:** the modals lack Figma's divider lines under the header and above the footer. Modal width (540px) and button heights also differ slightly from the frames.
- **Choices I made:**
  - Role colours are Admin red, Editor blue, Viewer grey, taken from Figma.
  - The log viewer is dark and monospace, because the spec says terminal-style; Figma shows a light list.
  - I added the "System Overview" heading and "Last updated" line from Figma.
  - The font is Inter if it's installed, otherwise the system font. Neither package provides one.

**Other changes:**
- The Angular 19 project was generated around the existing `package.json`. The old lockfile had pulled in Angular 21, so I regenerated it.
- I raised Angular's per-component stylesheet warning from 4 kB to 6 kB, because the dashboard stylesheet was 26 bytes over.
- "My Profile" does nothing, because there is no profile page.
